notes: Three university-level documents (students page, instructors page, IT best practices); no school or computing policy. Coders agreed on document stance and most unit codes. Disagreements: modality of 'expects' sentences (A must, B should; resolved to should); policy type for borderline units (instructor-balance sentence P83 vs UNCOVERED resolved to UNCOVERED because P83 was a stretch; 'no UNLV-wide policy' P56 vs UNCOVERED resolved to UNCOVERED; entering assignment/exam answers P03 vs P20 resolved to P20; supported-tools sentence P50 vs P92 resolved to P92; P10 vs P04 for contacting the instructor resolved to P10); actor and phase on a few units, settled by re-reading the sentence. unit_stance differences (restrict vs prohibit for misconduct, neutral vs permit) were resolved toward the less strong reading when the unit alone does not ban or allow. Coder-only units: two analogy-to-citation units from A were dropped as duplicates of the acknowledgment sentence; A's default-to-disclose, enterprise-tool definition and validate-the-source units were kept; B's prior-permission, email/code example and Financial/HCM units were kept. The reconciler added one unit neither coder had (understand data handling).
